- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 03:09
- [USER] User asked about the difference between modern Greek and ancient Greek.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Modern Greek is the language spoken today in Greece, Cyprus, and other parts of the Greek diaspora; it evolved from Ancient Greek, which was spoken from around the 9th century BCE to the end of the 4th century CE.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The main differences between Modern Greek and Ancient Greek are:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Vocabulary: Modern Greek has a different vocabulary than Ancient Greek, with many loanwords from other languages such as Turkish and French.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Grammar: Modern Greek has a simplified grammar compared to Ancient Greek, with fewer cases and declensions.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Pronunciation: Modern Greek has a different pronunciation from Ancient Greek, with some sounds and accents changing over time.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Spelling: Modern Greek uses a different alphabet from Ancient Greek, with some letters having different sounds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, while Modern Greek evolved from Ancient Greek, it has changed significantly over time, reflecting different historical and cultural influences.
- [USER] User expressed interest in whether people in Greece today still learn Ancient Greek in school.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, in Greece, Ancient Greek is still taught in schools as part of the national curriculum.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students learn the language, literature, and history of Ancient Greece to better understand the country's heritage and culture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study of Ancient Greek is optional for students, and not all schools offer it as a subject.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some private schools and universities offer more intensive courses in Ancient Greek, which can be helpful for students studying fields such as archaeology, history, classics, or philosophy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For most Greeks, the use of Ancient Greek is mostly limited to liturgy, some legal terms, and the names of organizations, streets, and places that still retain the Ancient Greek names.
- [USER] User found the information about Ancient Greek in schools to be cool and asked for common Ancient Greek phrases or words still used today.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common Ancient Greek phrases and words still used in Modern Greek include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Γεια σου (Yia sou) - Hello
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Ευχαριστώ (Efharisto) - Thank you
